headline: New Year Reflection—celebrating growth and setting intentions for the year ahead
universal_truth: Transition points invite reflection; the turn of the year is a natural time to look back and forward
fun_facts: Cultures worldwide have celebrated new year transitions for thousands of years
Written reflections are more powerful than mental ones for insight and commitment
Small specific intentions outperform vague resolutions
discussion_questions: What are you most proud of from this past year?
What did you learn about yourself?
What do you want to be true by next New Year?

hook.script: A new year begins. This moment of transition is ancient—humans have always paused here to look back and forward. Let's use this lesson for intentional reflection on where you've been and where you're going.

cliff.script: Most resolutions fail by February. What makes some new year intentions actually work?

options.text: Specific and small beats vague and grand—'exercise daily' fails while 'walk 10 minutes after lunch' succeeds; systems over goals; identity over behavior
options.response: Exactly. Don't resolve to 'learn more'—commit to 'one lesson every morning.' Specific, small, tied to routine. That's how new years actually change lives.
Willpower helps but depletes. Systems that don't require willpower work better long-term...

fact1.title: Celebrate What Was
fact1.script: Before looking forward, honor what's behind you. What did you accomplish this year? What did you survive? What did you learn? Take a moment to genuinely appreciate your past year's journey.

fact2.title: Release What Weighs
fact2.script: What from this year do you want to leave behind? Grudges, regrets, habits that don't serve you? Symbolically release them. The new year is a chance to travel lighter.

fact3.title: Plant Seeds Forward
fact3.script: What do you want to be true by next New Year? Not vague wishes—specific outcomes. Write them down. These become the seeds you'll nurture through the year ahead.

wisdom.script: Here's the wisdom for the new year: You don't have to be a new person. You just have to be a slightly better one, consistently. Small improvements compound into transformation.

outro.script: Happy New Year. May this year bring growth, curiosity, and joy. I'll be here every day to learn alongside you. Let's make it a good one.

growTrack.title: New Year Ritual - Reflect and Intend
growTrack.learning_objective: Complete a structured new year reflection
growTrack.activity: Write three things you're proud of from this year. Write one thing you're releasing. Write three specific intentions for the new year. Share one intention with someone who can support you.
